definition: Deliberately lowering an animation FILE's overall keyframe sample rate from a default (Moon Animator's default is 60) down to a stated specific value (24) is named directly as a stylistic choice — not a mistake or a performance compromise — to make a 3D Roblox character animation read with a more 'choppy', hand-drawn/2D-anime-adjacent quality.
purpose: Give a whole animation clip a deliberately lower, steppier sample rate as a genre/style dial (2D-anime-adjacent 'choppy' versus smooth 3D default), analogous to a hand-drawn production's own frame-rate conventions, but applied as a single project-wide setting rather than per-layer.
visible_effect: The same authored motion plays back with visibly larger, more discrete steps between poses at 24fps than at 60fps, reading as more stepped/hand-drawn rather than continuously smooth.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: The source's own direct claim: lowering the rate 'is going to look pretty good' as a deliberate choppy aesthetic, framed as an available creative option rather than a technical limitation to avoid. The same creator's later, more advanced video in this batch restates this far more forcefully as a near-universal community convention rather than merely an option: '60 is way too smooth... it just makes the animations look kind of CG or really weird... 99% of the time you want to keep this at 24 when you're making your Roblox animations, it's the best... I probably haven't really met that many animators who even animate at 60' (video 70 @ 08:09–09:05) — the same source restating and strengthening the claim seven months later, not a second independent creator confirming it.
physical_interpretation: None — a deliberate stylistic sample-rate choice, not a physical claim.
use_cases: an anime-style or stylized character animation wanting a hand-drawn-adjacent stepped read rather than a smooth default 3D feel

matching a target platform/genre convention (this batch's own `hand_drawn_layer_hold_rate_convention_by_layer_type`, video 63, describes actual hand-drawn TV anime running its CHARACTER layer at roughly 8-12 unique drawings/second — 24fps sits well above that, so this is a lighter step toward the same stylistic direction, not an attempt to literally match it)
non_use_cases: a realistic or default-feeling 3D character animation, where the project's normal sample rate should stay smooth
an animation whose motion detail genuinely needs the higher rate to read correctly (fast, fine, or subtle movements), where dropping to 24fps could lose information the smooth default preserves
interactions: differential_frame_rate_per_layer_for_performance_and_style (W06-55) — a sibling but distinct axis: that entry mixes MULTIPLE simultaneous rates across different layers within one real-time scene (60fps character, 30fps effects); this entry lowers the ENTIRE clip's own sample rate uniformly as a single project-wide setting, a coarser and simpler version of the same underlying idea

hand_drawn_layer_hold_rate_convention_by_layer_type (video 63, this batch) — the 2D production convention (8-12fps character drawings within a 24fps deliverable) this entry's 24fps choice gestures toward without literally reaching; worth reading together as two different distances from the same hand-drawn-anime reference point

low_field_of_view_reads_cinematic (video 67, this batch, enriched by this same video) — a sibling simple, single-scalar-setting stylistic dial from the same source video, both directly and immediately authorable with no new capability

style_variations.anime: the source states this explicitly as a way to get an anime-adjacent choppy look inside an otherwise smooth 3D rig pipeline
style_variations.realistic: contraindicated — a realistic character animation would normally want the smoother default rate, not a deliberately steppier one

cadence_representation: Directly and fully authorable today: Cadence's project has a single declared frame rate the same way Moon Animator's timeline does, so deliberately choosing a lower project rate (or, more precisely, a coarser effective sample rate via sparser keying, since Cadence's own timeline is not a fixed-fps sample grid the way Moon Animator's export is) is reachable with existing tools. No preset currently frames 'choose a lower effective rate for a choppy 2D-adjacent style' as a named option.
control_surface: `set_project_props` (or equivalent project-settings authoring) could already set a target frame rate; ordinary sparser keyframe spacing already achieves an equivalent choppier read without changing a declared rate at all.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Directly measurable: `ai/motion.js keyDensity`/`sampleMotion` already reports effective key spacing, so a clip's declared or effective sample rate is already visible in existing measurements — nothing new required, only a convention for what counts as a deliberately 'choppy' target rate.
generation_or_modification_methods: Ordinary keyframe authoring or a project frame-rate setting already reaches this; no preset proposes a target 'choppy' rate automatically.
failure_modes: lowering the rate on an animation whose important motion detail needs the higher sample rate to read correctly, losing information rather than gaining style

applying this project-wide when only specific layers (per `differential_frame_rate_per_layer_for_performance_and_style`) were meant to be affected, over-applying a coarser rate to content that didn't need it
roblox_considerations: Directly relevant and directly named in a Roblox/Moon Animator authoring context: the timeline FPS setting the source describes is a real, exposed control in the exact tool Cadence targets parity with, so matching or exceeding this exact capability (a settable target export/sample rate) is a concrete Moon-parity data point.
performance_implications: A lower keyframe sample rate for the same clip duration means fewer total keyframes, a minor authoring/storage saving; no meaningful runtime cost difference for an already-baked `AnimationTrack`.
examples: 'the default is 60, but if you want your animation to look a little more choppy, you can set this to 24, and it's also going to look pretty good — you can go ahead and test that out' (video @ 01:31–01:39), confirmed in this session's frame at t=01:20 showing Moon Animator's timeline-settings panel with the per-part track rows
evidence_status: video 68: https://youtu.be/267aFypaeWU (Nisky, "Roblox ANIMATION Guide #1 - Moon Animator") @ 01:31–01:39 — the presenter states the specific default and alternative values and the intended stylistic effect directly. video 70: https://youtu.be/EM9u4gIHoRg (the SAME creator's later Blender advanced guide, not an independent second source) @ 08:09–09:05 — restates and strengthens the same claim as a near-universal Roblox-animator convention over 60fps, gathered in this same W07 batch session; experimental until validated, and note this specific numeric convention rests on one creator's account across two videos rather than genuinely independent corroboration
